Tom / Ava —

Thanks again for the call this morning. To run a tight Dedicated sizing estimate for ApolloEdge (given the bursty inference pattern you described), we need a brief, structured snapshot of real traffic plus a few clarifying answers. I attached a lightweight template but below is the short survey you can paste answers into:

1) Typical concurrent active sessions at peak (per region):
   - Example: us-west: 560 sessions, eu-west: 80 sessions
2) Peak sustained QPS and peak burst QPS (5-minute window):
3) Prompt length distribution (percent buckets) and average response token length for each API surface (chat vs. generate vs. embeddings) — a short histogram is ideal.
4) Percent of requests that require full-context (long KV cache) vs. stateless single-shot prompts.
5) P99 latency SLO target per call type and any hard maximums.
6) Any nightly batch or bulk jobs (yes/no); if yes, attach sample job payload sizes.

If you can return the template or a CSV export of a representative day (UTC) we'll plug that into our sizing model and come back with GPU pool estimates, expected queueing at different SLAs, and fallback routing recommendations.

Timeline: if we get data by Tuesday EOD (your timezone), we can deliver a first-pass dimensioning on Thursday.

Thanks — simple answers ok, we can follow up with a short call for clarifications.

— Sergio

Appreciate the checklist. I exported a 24h sample from Fri (attached). Quick answers inline:

1) Peak concurrent active sessions (local breakout):
   - us-west: 420 active sessions (peak 09:00–10:00 PDT)
   - eu-west: 120 active sessions (peak 16:00–17:00 CEST)
2) Peak sustained QPS / peak burst QPS:
   - sustained QPS (5m): 320 QPS
   - 5m burst peak: 1,400 QPS (we see short spikes when vendors push batch updates)
3) Prompt length distribution (chat):
   - <64 tokens: 45%
   - 64–256 tokens: 35%
   - 256–1024 tokens: 15%

   Average response: ~180 tokens (chat), ~90 tokens (single-shot generate)

5) P99 latency SLO: 250ms for single-shot generate; 450ms for chat (we can tolerate up to 800ms during nightly batch windows)
6) Nightly batch jobs: yes — hourly ingestion jobs that hit the model for classification (~50k short calls over 2 hours).

I've attached the csv (session id, timestamp, prompt_len, resp_len, call_type) and telemetry snapshot for a typical day. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk the file.

Marissa / Sergio / Tom —

Thanks — quick conversion guidance so we’re aligned:

- For the model family ApolloEdge referenced (M40-like open family at 8-bit quant): assume ~75 tokens/sec per vGPU for long-context chat with typical attention optimizations. Short single-shot generations are ~240 tokens/sec per vGPU.
- For sizing the burst: if you want 99th percentile < 450ms for chat during spikes, we model queueing using a concurrency target where each active session consumes approx 1–2 vGPU-equivalent threads depending on KV cache residency.

Example calc based on Tom’s numbers (ballpark):
   Peak sustained QPS 320 with average response 180 tokens -> total token/sec = 57,600 -> at 240 tokens/sec per vGPU ≈ 240 vGPU-sec -> about 10 vGPUs sustaining (ignores batching savings)
   Burst spike 1,400 QPS (same avg resp) -> token/sec = 252,000 -> raw vGPU need ≈ 1,050 vGPU-sec -> with batching and short prompt optimization we can shave 3–4x; still implies a large transient pool or aggressive overprovisioning policy.

Action items for ApolloEdge to help accuracy:
 1) Send avg context length for the 18% multi-turn sessions (tokens).
 2) Mark whether batch pushes can be scheduled/staggered or are synchronous user-visible.
 3) Confirm any hard max latency for embedding calls (rare).

Tom — if you can add the two numbers above we’ll run the dimensioner and propose: dedicated baseline pool, hot burst pool config, and fallback to hosted tier for extreme spikes.

— Karthik

Tom / Ava —

Great data — thanks. Per Karthik’s ask we ran a first-pass dimensioning using the Friday export and a conservative batching profile. I attached a short executive note that summarizes the recommendation. Highlights:

- Baseline dedicated pool: 12 vGPUs (handles sustained 320 QPS with <350ms median latency after batching)
- Hot burst pool: elastic hot pool sized to 60 vGPUs (handles typical burst shape with 2–3x batching benefit); recommend autoscale policy that pre-warms based on vendor push windows (we can do time-based pre-warm or event hooks)
- Nightly batch window: schedule into a dedicated low-priority queue to avoid impacting customer-facing sessions; we estimate this needs an additional 6 vGPUs if run concurrently.
- KV-cache guidance: for the 18% multi-turn sessions, if average context length > 2,500 tokens we should consider a different model partitioning to reduce occupancy.

Next steps:
1) Tom — can you confirm avg context length for multi-turn sessions and whether batch pushes are schedulable? (EOD Wed preferred)
2) Redwood to run a second-pass with your preferred batching factor (we used x3) and deliver a cost/latency tradeoff table.
3) Quick 30-min call Thurs to review canary & fallback options.

I’ll loop in Account Exec (Marissa) for contractual sizing and Laura for onboarding notes once we lock numbers.

Thanks — we’ll hold the first-pass open for two days while we refine.

— Sergio
